newsitem.title: FRANCE: France backs airdrop, still wants full Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: France backs airdrop, still wants full Zaire force.

text.p: France said on Thursday it was prepared to join a proposed airdrop of food into eastern Zaire, but added that the numbers of refugees still made a U.N.-sponsored multinational ground force necessary.
But as Paris announced its support for airdrops, Zaire said it would not permit them.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing Paris had considered Canadian proposals for an airdrop, and "we immediately assured Canadian authorities that we were prepared to participate in such an operation".

But Zaire said it would not allow food airdrops, citing concern over the safety of the displaced people roaming the Zaire jungle and the fact that the airdrops would be staged from neighbouring countries it accuses of aggression.

But Rummelhardt said France still backed a multi-national intervention force to bring help to thousands of Rwandan refugees adrift in eastern Zaire, despite a cooling of enthusiasm among other countries for the project.

"Given the magnitude of the humanitarian problem...we remain convinced that Resolution 1080 must be fully implemented until aid organisations on the ground obtain free access to populations in need," Rummelhardt added.
Security Council Resolution 1080 set up a multinational Canadian-led force to protect refugees caught in fighting in eastern Zaire and secure food aid corridors.
But support for the plan has been waning since more than half a million refugees the force was supposed to help returned to their homes in Rwanda earlier this month.
Rwanda has said the force was no longer needed.
